_about: Hand-picked 'local favourites'. Edit freely: each entry becomes a page at /favourites/<slug>/, a star on the atlas and a card on the homepage. Set "draft": true to hide an entry, and "approx": true when the pin is only roughly placed. coords are [longitude, latitude].

items.name: Mt Buffalo Chalet
items.blurb: The grand old guesthouse on top of Mt Buffalo is waking up after two decades.
body: Perched on the edge of Mt Buffalo’s granite plateau, the heritage-listed chalet sat closed for around twenty years. It’s now coming back to life in stages: outdoor-education school camps are already running, with a café and, later, heritage accommodation on the way.
Make a day of it — walk out to the lookouts over the Gorge, then cool off at Lake Catani just up the road.
items.tip: The café’s opening slipped into October 2026, so check it’s open before you drive up.

items.name: Mystic Bike Park
items.blurb: 50-plus km of purpose-built trails in the pines, four minutes from town.
body: Bright’s home trails cover everything from a flat, groomed family loop right off the car park to technical singletrack, flow lines and jump trails higher up the hill.
Pedal up any day of the year, or ride the uplift shuttle on weekends and holidays. Bike and e-bike hire, lessons and guided rides are run from the trailhead on Coronation Avenue.
items.tip: New to dirt? Start on Hot Wheels, the easy trail straight from the car park.

items.name: Jenvey’s swimming hole
items.blurb: A locals’ swim in the Ovens River, a short walk from the middle of Bright.
body: Tucked along the Ovens River off Mountbatten Avenue, Jenvey’s is a summer favourite for a quick dip after a hot ride or walk.
It’s also where whitewater kayaking and packrafting trips through the Bright gorge set off, so don’t be surprised to see paddlers launching on a busy day.
items.tip: River levels and currents change quickly — skip it after heavy rain, and always check before jumping in.

items.name: Bright Brewery
items.blurb: A Bright institution: mountain-made beer and a tasting paddle on Gavan Street.
body: Grab a paddle of their MountainCrafted core range at the Gavan Street brewpub and you’ll see why it’s the default post-ride stop in town.
Beer nerds can book a guided tour of Fred’s Shed, the production brewery 1.5 km out of town, which runs on the last Friday of each month and on Fridays in Victorian school holidays.
items.tip: Tours start at 3 pm and include a tasting paddle — book ahead.

items.name: Rail trail: Bright to Porepunkah
items.blurb: The flattest, friendliest 6 km in the valley — on two wheels.
body: This sealed stretch of the Murray to Mountains Rail Trail follows the old railway from Bright to Porepunkah: off-road, almost dead flat, with bridges and river views the whole way.
Feeling keen? The full trail runs for more than 100 km to Wangaratta, with branches to Beechworth and the King Valley. The ride on to Myrtleford has big views of Mt Buffalo.
items.tip: It gets busy on sunny weekends — go early, or after lunch on a weekday.

items.name: Lake Catani
items.blurb: Swim, paddle or camp beside a snow-gum lake high on the Buffalo plateau.
body: Lake Catani is the summer hub of Mt Buffalo: swimming, canoeing and kayaking on a calm alpine lake (no motorboats), with picnic spots under the snow gums.
The campground beside it is the only one in the national park you can drive into, with hot showers and walk-in and drive-in sites.
items.tip: Summer camping runs from November to April and must be booked in advance.

items.name: Big Hill Mountain Bike Park
items.blurb: Three decades of hand-cut, rough-and-rowdy singletrack, right in town.
body: One of the pioneers of Australian mountain biking. Big Hill has around 40–50 km of mostly hand-built singletrack, from mellow cross-country loops to serious downhill lines.
It’s built and looked after entirely by volunteers from Team Mount Beauty, and the trailhead is a few hundred metres from the town’s shops, cafés and bakery.
items.tip: There’s parking and toilets at the trailhead. Consider chipping in to the club that maintains the trails.

items.name: Milawa Cheese Company
items.blurb: Handmade cheese in the old Milawa butter factory, since 1988.
body: Work your way through a tasting of their cow and goat cheeses, made and matured by hand on site. The old butter factory also houses a kitchen, Milawa Bread and the Wood Park Wines cellar door.
It’s the natural first stop on a lazy loop of the Milawa gourmet region.
items.tip: Open every day of the year except Christmas Day.

items.name: Old Beechworth Gaol
items.blurb: A granite gaol with 140 years of stories — and strong links to the Kelly story.
body: Built from local granite, the gaol held prisoners from 1864 until it closed in 2004. Guided tours take you through the courtyard, cell blocks and solitary cells.
In Victorian school holidays and on long weekends, family tours let kids aged 6–12 join the prison muster, try on manacles and see replica Kelly Gang armour up close.
items.tip: Daily tours run through the day and last about 45 minutes. No pets on tours.

items.name: Dargo Hotel
items.blurb: An 1898 bush pub at the bottom of the Dargo High Plains Road.
body: Little has changed at the Dargo Hotel since the 1890s, and that’s the point. It’s the classic meeting spot for four-wheel drivers heading up to the high plains, with meals, a beer garden, and motel rooms, cabins and bunk rooms out back.
Check the track closures on the atlas before heading uphill: the Dargo High Plains Road closes seasonally.

items.name: Oriental Claims
items.blurb: Walk through 30-metre cliffs carved by one of the world’s biggest gold-sluicing operations.
body: For more than 50 years, miners blasted the hillsides along Livingstone Creek with high-pressure water to wash out the gold, leaving behind dramatic sculpted cliffs.
Short loop walks, including Ah Fong’s Loop and the Pioneer Claim Loop (about 45 minutes each), tell the stories of the Chinese and European miners who worked here.
items.tip: Toilets and picnic tables at the start — bring lunch.

items.name: Jamieson Brewery & Grill
items.blurb: A riverside pub and grill on the Goulburn at Jamieson.
body: Set in parkland gardens with the Goulburn River at the back door, this long-running venue is a handy lunch stop on the way into the Jamieson high country.
items.tip: DRAFT — confirm whether beer is still brewed on site, and current opening days, before publishing.
